svg.title: Give the CA its different address — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Give the CA its different address
TLS-CA01 · RHEL 9 local console · Bash
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-ca01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
nmcli -t -f NAME connection show --active
LAB_CONNECTION='Wired connection 1'
sudo nmcli connection modify "$LAB_CONNECTION" ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 10.90.0.20/24
ipv4.gateway '' ipv4.dns '' ipv4.never-default yes
sudo nmcli connection up "$LAB_CONNECTION"
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname tls-ca01.lab.example.test
ip -br address
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The CA Ethernet interface shows 10.90.0.20/24.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Open the TLS-CA01 console, not TLS-APP01, and sign in as learner.
2. Run the first command and put its exact connection profile into LAB_CONNECTION, just as you did on
the application server.
3. Paste the remaining lines, then check the address.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
